ownership_reason: Only the gold chooses how many terms of the Taylor series are summed and sums them; hop 1 folds the sign, hop 2 chooses between the logarithmic form (above 0.167) and the series, hops 3 and 4 pass the number along. Once the series has been cut too early its value cannot be corrected by a caller, and no one-line change above the gold restores accuracy on (0.036, 0.097]: the logarithmic form loses up to 12 ulps there and 0.05 is off by more than the tolerance under both forms. The convention is pinned outside the gold: FastMath.atanh, beside the facade, evaluates its small-argument series in the same four tiers (to a^17, a^13, a^9 and a^5); the FastMath class javadoc states that almost all operations are accurate to about 0.5 ulp; DSCompiler.asinh and function.Asinh call the facade for their values; testSinhAsinh checks asinh through the same chain and gold to 3e-16 for arguments of at least 0.1, testTanhAtanh checks atanh's tiered series, testHyperbolic checks the sinh used by the trigger's round trip.
